quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance when driving behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers pull behind large vehicles before passing them.
Because following too closely will catch you in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles pulling trailers cannot see you if you drive directly behind them. Increase your following distance to see around the sides and watch the road ahead.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you expect?

options.text: Beep your horn.
The child to have total control of the bicycle.
The unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: The unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable. They often change direction suddenly without warning. Children and bicycles are small and can be hard to see.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is good defensive driving.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slower than usual in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive too slowly and block normal traffic flow, you can be cited.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This lets other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians know what you plan to do.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If fog is so thick you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: When may you drive in an HOV lane?

options.text: When you are driving faster than traffic.
When you are driving slower than traffic.
When your vehicle has more than one person.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle has more than one person.
questions.explanation: Some highways reserve the left lane for vehicles with multiple people. These High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lanes are marked with signs and diamond symbols on the pavement.

questions.question: If you must park in an unusual location, what should you do?

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for making sure your parked vehicle is not a hazard. Wherever you park, make sure other drivers can see your car coming from any direction.

questions.question: What does interstate driving require of drivers?

options.text: The ability to safely drive at higher speeds.
Constant alertness.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert at all times and be able to drive at high speeds safely.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a large commercial vehicle?

options.text: Follow closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Do not stay beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reduces all the abilities you need to drive safely. It goes from your stomach to your blood, then to other parts of your body. Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and skill.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, what should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for them to cross the street.
Pull right and go around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for them to cross the street.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until the intersection is clear before you go.

questions.question: How can you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to know where traffic behind you is located.

questions.question: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on four-way flashers and continue.
Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
Turn on high beams and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If heavy smoke covers the road, slow down immediately, drive as far right as possible, and stop off the road. Then check if it is safe to continue. Some types of smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or be dangerous.

questions.question: When may you pass on the right shoulder?

options.text: When the car in front is turning.
When the car in front is driving too slowly.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right only when it is safe. You can never drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars on the right move first.
You have the right-of-way.
Let other traffic pass before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic pass before you go.
questions.explanation: When you see this sign, you must yield. Slow down and let all vehicles and pedestrians cross your path first. Stop if you need to before moving forward.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks your front wheels and makes steering impossible.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks your front wheels and makes steering impossible.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock your front wheels. When this happens, you lose the ability to steer. Slow down before you need to brake so you do not have to brake hard.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Wait for the warning lights to stop flashing.
Check for another train coming.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: A second train may be coming on another track. Do not move until all gates are up and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you sleepy.
Over-the-counter drugs do not affect driving if you take the right dose.
Doctor-prescribed medicines are always safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you sleepy.
questions.explanation: All medicines—prescription or over-the-counter—can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy. Know how your medicine affects you before you drive.

questions.question: When bad weather or darkness requires your lights on while driving, use:

options.text: Your parking lights.
Your high beams.
Your low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect back and cause glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: A broken yellow line in the center of a road means:

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
No one can pass.
Anyone can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anyone can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road has curves ahead.

questions.question: A driver turning left must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming traffic going straight or turning right.
Cars passing you.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming traffic going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to all oncoming traffic, including bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: Stopping distance and crash severity:

options.text: Get shorter as speed increases.
Are not affected by speed.
Get longer and worse as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get longer and worse as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speed means longer stopping distance and more serious crashes. Keep more space between you and other cars as you drive faster.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes:

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use the side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors do not show blind spots. Always turn your head to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to police:

options.text: Only if you are in a crash.
If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped for a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: Always carry proof of insurance. Show it to an officer after any traffic stop or crash.

questions.question: You should not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: In any situation.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: In any situation.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, only enter an intersection if you can clear it before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can go either way in this lane.
Traffic is coming from both directions.
You are entering a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is coming from both directions.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is moving both ways.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or back so they can see you.
Keep the same speed.
Stay in their blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or back so they can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move up or drop back so the driver can see you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows there is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.
